items.title: UK inflation rises to 3.5%, its highest in almost a year
items.why: Prices in the UK rose 3.5% in the year to September, up from 3.1% in August and above the 3.4% most economists expected, the Office for National Statistics said on 21 October. Petrol and diesel drove the rise; diesel is at its highest since July 2022.
items.matters: Motor fuel prices are up nearly 30% on a year ago, the ONS says, raising costs for households and businesses.

items.title: UN says world heads for 2.6C warming even if pledges are met
items.why: The UN Environment Programme's Emissions Gap Report, published on 21 October, says fully delivering countries' climate pledges would still mean about 2.6C of warming by 2100; current policies point to 2.8C. Global emissions were about 58.4 billion tonnes in 2025, roughly level with 2024.
items.matters: UNEP says emissions must fall 18% by 2030 to keep the overshoot above 1.5C as small as possible.

items.title: LeBron James's 76ers spoil Knicks' title celebration as NBA season opens
items.why: The Philadelphia 76ers beat the champion New York Knicks 106-100 at Madison Square Garden on 20 October, the NBA's opening night, after the Knicks raised their first title banner in 53 years. LeBron James, in a record 24th season, had 14 points on his 76ers debut; Tyrese Maxey scored 28.

items.title: South Korea's Kospi jumps more than 4% as chip shares rebound
items.why: Seoul's main share index rose more than 4% on Wednesday morning, a day after falling nearly 4%, with Samsung Electronics and SK hynix up about 7%. Strong US tech earnings revived confidence, and the exchange briefly paused programme buying for the first time since August.
items.matters: Korean chipmakers are a bellwether for global spending on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Skeleton in Roman coffin at Westminster Abbey was probably a Saxon abbot
items.why: A skeleton found in a fourth-century Roman sarcophagus at Westminster Abbey in London is most likely Ælfwig, an abbot who died around 1020, the abbey's consultant archaeologist Warwick Rodwell argues in the Journal of the British Archaeological Association. Radiocarbon dating places the man's death between 987 and 1052.
items.matters: The coffin's inscription names a fourth-century Briton, so it was reused centuries later; Rodwell names a second candidate, Wulfnoth.

items.title: Musk says SpaceX and Tesla have formed committees to consider merging
items.why: Elon Musk said on 20 October that SpaceX and Tesla have each set up committees of independent directors to discuss combining, calling it 'a good idea' but not certain. SpaceX, which listed in June, reported a $4.4 billion quarterly profit on revenue up 161% to $14.6 billion.
items.matters: Al Jazeera says the two firms are worth about $3.5 trillion together, so a deal would be the largest merger ever.

items.title: PSG beat Barcelona 4-2, ending their winning start to the season
items.why: Champions League holders Paris Saint-Germain beat Barcelona 4-2 in Paris on 20 October, with late goals from Vitinha and Fabián Ruiz after Lamine Yamal had made it 2-2. It ended Barcelona's run of 11 straight wins; PSG top the league phase with nine points.

items.title: Liverpool come from two goals down to beat Villarreal 4-3
items.why: Liverpool beat Villarreal 4-3 in the Champions League at Anfield on 20 October after trailing 2-0 within 29 minutes. Alexis Mac Allister scored twice, with Ronald Araújo and substitute Florian Wirtz also scoring; 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha set up two goals.
items.matters: Liverpool and the holders, Paris Saint-Germain, lead the table with nine points from three games each.

items.title: Netflix shares fall after weak forecast and cut to advertising outlook
items.why: Netflix said on 20 October its third-quarter revenue rose 12% to $12.9 billion, in line with forecasts, but it predicted lower fourth-quarter profit than analysts expected and cut its 2026 advertising revenue forecast to about $2.7 billion from $3 billion. Shares fell nearly 6% in after-hours trading.
items.matters: The company recently cut about 1,000 jobs, around 6% of staff, and replaced its content chief, Reuters reports.

items.changed: Updated: electoral court meets Meta and both campaigns over equal treatment online
items.title: Brazil's electoral court meets Meta and both campaigns before Sunday's run-off
items.why: A judge at Brazil's Superior Electoral Court met Meta and lawyers for President Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro on Tuesday over an order to treat both candidates equally online. Lula's campaign says its posts were restricted; Meta denies favouring either side and blames technical faults. The run-off is on 25 October.
items.matters: It tests how far courts can police tech platforms during an election.

items.title: US approves first drug of its kind for chronic hepatitis B
items.why: The US Food and Drug Administration approved GSK's Hibsago (bepirovirsen) on 20 October for some adults with chronic hepatitis B, given alongside existing antivirals. In two trials, 19% of patients still had the virus under control six months after stopping all treatment; none did on placebo.
items.matters: GSK says more than 240 million people live with chronic hepatitis B, which causes about 1.1 million deaths a year.

items.title: US regulator approves Boeing's largest 737 Max after years of delays
items.why: The US Federal Aviation Administration certified the Boeing 737 Max 10 on 20 October, almost a decade after the jet was unveiled in 2017. It seats up to 230 passengers. More than 30 customers have ordered 1,555, and Boeing expects deliveries to begin in the coming months.
items.matters: It is the first airliner certified under all of a 2020 US safety law passed after two 737 Max crashes.

items.title: Rare Arctic beluga whale filmed off Ireland's Donegal coast
items.why: A beluga whale, normally found in Arctic and sub-Arctic waters, was filmed by drone in Donegal Bay, north-west Ireland, on 17 October. The Irish Whale and Dolphin Group says it is only the second validated beluga record in Irish waters, after one off County Antrim in 2015.
items.matters: The group says the adult appears healthy, and Arctic species such as belugas and narwhals are being seen more often off Ireland.

items.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three tankers hit mines near Hormuz
items.why: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Tuesday that naval mines set two tankers on fire in the Strait of Hormuz and a third, carrying over 2 million barrels of crude, exploded south of the strait. They said the ships took routes Iran calls unauthorised. The claims have not been independently confirmed.
items.matters: Before the war about a fifth of the world's oil passed through the strait.

items.changed: Updated: Witkoff lands in St Petersburg; Kremlin says Putin receives him on Wednesday
items.title: Witkoff arrives in St Petersburg for talks with Putin on Ukraine
items.why: US envoy Steve Witkoff landed in St Petersburg after talks with Ukraine's President Zelensky in Oslo. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Putin would receive him at the Constantine Palace on Wednesday morning. A US official told Axios he carries an updated proposal to end the war.
items.matters: It is the latest US attempt to bring Russia and Ukraine towards direct talks.

items.title: Italy sends 500 soldiers to Milan and toughens protest laws after riots
items.why: Italy's cabinet approved a decree on Tuesday sending 500 extra soldiers to Milan until the end of the year, after weekend riots and looting during cost-of-living protests. It creates an offence of 'violent participation in a demonstration', punishable by up to five years in prison.
items.matters: It follows similar fuel-price unrest in France, where night curfews remain in parts of Paris and Lyon.

items.title: Christina Applegate says doctors now find she does not have MS
items.why: US actor Christina Applegate, 54, who announced a multiple sclerosis diagnosis in 2021, said on her podcast MeSsy on 20 October that her doctor has told her she does not have the disease. She still has severe symptoms and says she is 'back at square one'.
items.matters: A Cedars-Sinai neurologist on the podcast said misdiagnosis of MS is fairly common, as there is no single test for it.

items.title: Arafat Minhas takes six wickets as Pakistan beat England by 87 runs
items.why: All-rounder Arafat Minhas scored 59 and took six wickets for 40 as Pakistan beat England by 87 runs in a one-day tri-series match in Rawalpindi, Pakistan, on 20 October. Pakistan made 302 for nine; England were bowled out for 215.

items.title: UN experts urge India to stop 'excessive force' against protesters
items.why: About two dozen independent UN human rights experts said on Tuesday that police used baton charges on unarmed students at protests in New Delhi and elsewhere. They cite reports that more than 7,000 people were detained. Protesters want India's chief election commissioner to resign over voter-list revisions.
items.matters: Critics say about 130 million names were removed from voter lists; the Election Commission says it removed ineligible voters.

items.changed: Updated: Bavuma made 179 and South Africa declared on 425 for nine
items.title: Bavuma's 179 puts South Africa on top in second Test
items.why: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma made a Test-best 179 on day three in Gqeberha on 20 October, after his side had slipped to 40 for four. South Africa declared on 425 for nine; Australia closed on 3 for one. Australia lead the three-match series 1-0.

items.changed: Updated: Brent settled lower on Tuesday after mediation reports, then rose again early Wednesday
items.title: Oil swings around $110 a barrel on Iran mediation reports
items.why: Brent crude touched $111.99 on Tuesday, its highest since May, then settled at $108.79 after reports of a Qatar-Pakistan plan to revive US-Iran talks, Reuters reported. Early on Wednesday it rose about 1.5% to around $110.40, AP said.
items.matters: Oil prices feed into fuel, heating and shipping costs around the world.

items.title: Rubio says US and India are 'very close' to a trade deal
items.why: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met India's Foreign Minister S Jaishankar in Mumbai on Tuesday, AP reports. Rubio said a deal is 'about as close as you can be' without signing. Talks have stalled for months over US tariffs and India's purchases of Russian oil.
items.matters: US tariffs on Indian goods reached 50% in 2025 before a February framework cut them to 18%.

items.title: Britain to fly RAF Typhoon jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthis
items.why: Britain's Ministry of Defence said on Tuesday that RAF Typhoons will fly defensive missions over Saudi Arabia against Houthi drones and missiles, after a Saudi request. They will not strike Houthi targets in Yemen. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting called the Houthi attacks 'absolutely despicable'.
items.matters: It deepens Britain's military role as Houthi strikes on Saudi cities, airports and oil sites continue.

items.changed: Updated: Iran tells mediator no talks before US meets its terms; Rubio calls a deal 'extremely difficult'
items.title: Iran tells Pakistan's army chief no US talks until demands met
items.why: Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, met Iran's president and top officials in Tehran on Tuesday, but no breakthrough was announced. Iranian media say Tehran wants the US to accept its seven conditions first, including lifting oil sanctions. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called a deal 'extremely difficult'.
items.matters: Talks centre on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil route, which Iran says stays shut until its terms are met.

items.title: Alberta votes by about three to one to stay in Canada
items.why: About 76% of voters in the western Canadian province of Alberta chose to remain in Canada in Monday's referendum, preliminary results show, with about 1.8 million votes counted. The rest backed starting a process towards a binding vote on leaving.
items.matters: Prime Minister Mark Carney said Albertans 'chose unity'; separatist campaigners say their push will continue.

items.title: US defence secretary Hegseth meets Netanyahu on unannounced Israel visit
items.why: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at an air base in southern Israel on Monday, Axios and Israeli media report; the Pentagon declined to comment. Netanyahu later released video of a call in which he told President Trump they have 'a job to finish'.
items.matters: It came a day after Trump endorsed Netanyahu for Israel's 27 October election and as Russia's foreign minister visited Tehran.

items.title: Suspected Chinese rocket debris falls on plantation in Indonesian Borneo
items.why: A large burnt metal piece, which police describe as up to nine metres long, was found on a palm oil plantation near Sampit, Central Kalimantan, on 19 October after residents heard a loud bang. Indonesia's research agency BRIN suspects it came from China's Zhuque-2E rocket. Nobody was hurt.
items.matters: ESA says injury risk from falling space debris is very low but rising as launches increase.

items.changed: Updated: winds up to 215 km/h; Batanes now under Signal No. 2
items.title: Batanes raised to storm Signal No. 2 as Super Typhoon Champi nears
items.why: Champi, named Rosal locally, had winds of 215 km/h and gusts of 265 km/h on Wednesday morning, about 845 km east of northern Luzon, the weather agency PAGASA says. It expects no landfall, but closest approach to Batanes on Thursday or Friday.
items.matters: Taiwan's weather agency expects heavy rain and waves of up to 6 metres in the north and east on Friday and Saturday.

items.title: Angel Reese's 30 points help Atlanta Dream level WNBA Finals
items.why: The Atlanta Dream beat the Golden State Valkyries 79-65 in San Francisco on Monday 19 October, levelling the best-of-seven WNBA Finals at 1-1. Angel Reese scored 30 points and took 16 rebounds. It was Atlanta's first Finals win, after losing all three of its previous Finals.
items.matters: Game 3 is in Atlanta on Wednesday 21 October.

items.title: US judge orders ex-OpenAI engineer held without bail in recording-device case
items.why: A US federal judge in San Francisco on Monday ordered Abdulrahman Alfozan, a Saudi former OpenAI engineer, held until trial, citing a 'significant' flight risk. He is charged with hiding a recording device in an OpenAI meeting room. Prosecutors cite help from Saudi officials; his lawyer denies he would flee.
items.matters: Prosecutors call the case a national security concern; the next hearing is on 6 November.

items.title: US approves immunotherapy that may spare some rectal cancer patients surgery
items.why: The US Food and Drug Administration gave accelerated approval on 19 October to GSK's immunotherapy Jemperli (dostarlimab) for a genetic type of locally advanced rectal cancer. In a 154-patient trial, almost three-quarters needed no surgery, radiation or chemotherapy after a median follow-up of two years, the FDA says.
items.matters: The subtype, called dMMR or MSI-H, is a small share of rectal cancers; the FDA says longer follow-up is still needed.

items.title: Japan launches probe to bring back samples from Mars moon Phobos
items.why: Japan's space agency JAXA launched its MMX probe on an H3 rocket from Tanegashima at 19:41 UTC on 19 October (04:41 Tuesday, Japan time). About 71 minutes later it was released into its planned orbit, Jiji Press reports. MMX should reach Mars in 2027 and return samples in 2031.
items.matters: No mission has yet brought back material from the Mars system; it may show how Mars's two small moons formed.

items.title: Portugal federation bans Ronaldo for 30 days over squad walkout
items.why: Portugal's football federation suspended captain Cristiano Ronaldo, 41, for 30 days and fined him €255 on 19 October for leaving the national team camp in Copenhagen after a dispute with coach Jorge Jesus. Reports say the ban is backdated to the start of October.
items.matters: He is expected to be available for Portugal's Nations League games in November if Jesus picks him.

items.title: Trump orders new women's health division at US National Institutes of Health
items.why: US President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Monday telling health officials to set up a women's health division at the National Institutes of Health within 90 days, plus a White House task force. First Lady Melania Trump led the effort; the order names no specific funding.
items.matters: Critics cited by Al Jazeera question how it will work after thousands of NIH staff were laid off and budgets cut.

items.title: US orders civilian government agencies to stop using China's DeepSeek AI
items.why: The US Department of Homeland Security has ordered federal civilian agencies to remove AI tools from Chinese company DeepSeek, including other firms' products built on its models. The order, made public on 19 October, does not cover the military, AFP reports.
items.matters: DHS says using the tools may send sensitive data to China; the two countries' leaders are due to meet next month.

items.title: Saudi Arabia postpones its 'Davos in the Desert' investment summit to 2027
items.why: The Future Investment Initiative, due in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, from 26 to 29 October, has been moved to 2027, organisers said on Monday. AFP and Reuters link the delay to Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, including on Riyadh's main airport. New dates have not been set.
items.matters: Expected speakers included the heads of BlackRock, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan; two other Saudi business events were also postponed.

items.title: Germany and Nvidia agree to work on AI for industry
items.why: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Nvidia chief Jensen Huang announced a partnership on 19 October at the first Invest in Germany summit in Berlin, aimed at AI models for factories and robots. Economy Minister Katherina Reiche says investors pledged more than €225 billion at the summit.
items.matters: Germany, Europe's largest economy, hopes AI can help revive its struggling carmakers and machinery makers.

items.title: Christiane Amanpour to leave CNN after 43 years
items.why: CNN's chief international anchor, Christiane Amanpour, 68, said on 19 October that she will leave the network after 43 years. Her daily CNN and PBS programmes end in late 2026; a weekly CNN International show continues until May, and she leaves in June 2027.
items.matters: It comes weeks after Paramount Skydance took over CNN's parent company; Amanpour did not mention the deal, AFP reports.

items.title: Ramaphosa tells South Africa to prepare for losing US trade benefits
items.why: South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa said on 19 October the country must prepare for possible exclusion from AGOA, the US scheme giving African goods duty-free access. He said the effect on jobs would be 'devastating'. Any exclusion from 1 January must be announced by 2 November.
items.matters: Carmakers' groups say about 86,000 South African jobs depend directly on the deal.

items.title: Four Salvadoran soldiers missing after gang ambush in Haiti
items.why: Gangs attacked an armoured vehicle of the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force on Sunday in Croix-des-Bouquets, near Haiti's capital, Port-au-Prince, El Salvador's military says. Four Salvadoran air force members escaped the burning vehicle but remain unaccounted for; helicopters sent to help came under fire.
items.matters: AP calls it the first major attack on the force, which has about 2,000 troops, just over a third of its target.

items.title: Pakistan confirms first polio case in Karachi since December 2024
items.why: Pakistan's polio programme confirmed on Monday that a six-month-old boy in Karachi East has wild poliovirus, the country's seventh case this year and Karachi's first since December 2024. Five of the seven cases are in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province and two in Sindh, which includes Karachi.
items.matters: A vaccination campaign from 2 to 8 November aims to reach nearly 24 million children under five in 97 districts.

items.title: Ruling on Senegal's Africa Cup of Nations appeal expected in late November
items.why: The Court of Arbitration for Sport said on 19 October it will rule on Senegal's appeal at the end of November, not within days as first signalled. Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 in January's final, but African football's governing body, CAF, later awarded Morocco the title.
items.matters: CAF ruled Senegal forfeited by walking off for 14 minutes in protest at a penalty; Senegal says the referee let play finish.

items.title: Benny Gantz quits Israel's election race eight days before the vote
items.why: Former army chief Benny Gantz said on Monday he will not run in Israel's 27 October election, after polls repeatedly put his Blue and White party below the 3.25% threshold needed to enter parliament. 'The responsibility is mine,' he said. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot called it a 'responsible' decision.
items.matters: Gantz was Netanyahu's main rival in three elections; his party's name will still appear on the ballot.

items.title: Europe's Euclid space telescope finds its first new comet
items.why: The European Space Agency says Euclid, built to map distant galaxies, has found a previously unknown comet, C/2026 S1 (Euclid), about 1.3 billion km from Earth. A University of Helsinki PhD student spotted it in September images; the Minor Planet Center confirmed it on 8 October.
items.matters: It suggests survey telescopes can spot comets far from the Sun, early enough for missions such as ESA's planned Comet Interceptor.

items.title: Exiled critic of Rwanda's President Kagame found killed in Uganda
items.why: A former Rwandan army sergeant who ran a popular YouTube channel criticising President Paul Kagame was found dead on 17 October in Mpigi district, near Uganda's capital, Kampala. Ugandan police said on Monday they had opened a murder case; no one has been arrested.
items.matters: Rwanda's government has not commented; Al Jazeera notes Rwandan authorities have been accused before of killing opponents abroad.

items.changed: Updated: toll rises to at least 73
items.title: Yemen officials say Houthi missiles killed at least 73 at army camp
items.why: Houthi ballistic missiles hit a government training camp near Ataq, in Shabwa province, southern Yemen, on Monday. A senior government official told AP at least 73 recruits were killed; the governor says more than 200 were wounded and some are missing. The Houthis said they targeted 'Saudi enemy' forces.
items.matters: AP calls it the deadliest strike since fighting in Yemen escalated in July.

items.title: Baby orangutan rescued from a flat near Mumbai returns to Indonesia
items.why: A young male Sumatran orangutan, found in an apartment in Thane, near Mumbai, India, in November 2024, was flown to Medan, Indonesia, on 19 October. He will go to a rescue centre in North Sumatra to learn climbing and foraging before any release, Indonesian officials say.
items.matters: India waived the cost of his care; five more young orangutans found in India's Odisha state in September may follow.

items.changed: Updated: the latest daily figures put the toll at 1,204
items.title: Bangladesh measles outbreak deaths pass 1,200, health officials say
items.why: Bangladesh's health directorate says more than 1,200 people, mostly children, have died with measles or measles-like symptoms this year; its latest daily figures put the toll at 1,204, including 1,100 suspected deaths. More than 215,000 suspected cases have been recorded since mid-March.

items.title: Kenyan court convicts cult leader Paul Mackenzie over 191 starvation deaths
items.why: A Kenyan court on Monday found pastor Paul Mackenzie and 28 others guilty of murdering 191 people, 190 of them children. Prosecutors said he told followers to starve themselves to 'meet Jesus' in Shakahola forest, on Kenya's coast. Sentencing is set for 6 November.
items.matters: Authorities say more than 400 people died in the forest; Mackenzie also faces separate terrorism and manslaughter charges.

items.changed: Updated: drone strike on Abyei market; local officials say at least 153 killed
items.title: Officials say drone strike on Abyei market killed at least 153
items.why: A drone hit Amiet market and a nearby fuel depot in Abyei, an area claimed by both Sudan and South Sudan, on Monday. Abyei's information minister says at least 153 people died and later put the toll above 220. He and South Sudan's government blame Sudan's army.
items.matters: A Sudanese army officer told AP the army targeted fuel bound for the paramilitary RSF and does not target civilians.

items.changed: Updated: death toll rises to at least five; storm easing
items.title: Storm Adam death toll in Spain rises to at least five
items.why: At least five people have died in floods from Storm Adam: three in the Valencia region, one in Catalonia and one in Andalusia, Italy's LaPresse agency reports. The Civil Guard says it has evacuated more than 2,100 people and rescued almost 500 in Valencia. The storm eased on Tuesday.
items.matters: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez was due in Oliva, the worst-hit town, on Tuesday; weather warnings remain in nine provinces.

items.changed: Updated: man charged and remanded in custody; her husband says she is stable
items.title: Man charged over car attack on Australian MP Helen Haines
items.why: Independent MP Helen Haines, 65, was hit by a four-wheel drive outside her office in Wangaratta, Victoria, on Monday. A 43-year-old man appeared in court on Wednesday charged with intentionally causing serious injury and harming a Commonwealth official, and was remanded in custody.
items.matters: Her husband says both her legs have been amputated and she is stable; police have not ruled out further charges.

items.changed: Updated: Nigeria confirms its first case; Kenya's total rises to nine
items.title: Nigeria confirms first Ebola case as Kenya's total rises to nine
items.why: Nigeria's health ministry said on 20 October that a woman who arrived in the capital, Abuja, from Uganda has Ebola; 44 contacts are being traced. Kenya confirmed its ninth case, all in one cluster. Congo has recorded more than 9,000 cases and 4,300 deaths, its health authorities say.
items.matters: There is no licensed vaccine for this Bundibugyo strain, and Africa CDC calls it the most widespread Ebola outbreak on record.

items.changed: Updated: police say the actor was not the gunmen's first target
items.title: Police say Tiger Shroff was not the gunmen's original target
items.why: Mumbai's Crime Branch says the men who fired at actor Tiger Shroff's car on 18 October first planned to attack another film star but found his security too tight. Three suspects arrested in Kota, Rajasthan, were brought to Mumbai on 21 October; Delhi Police arrested four more.

items.changed: Updated: a Bogotá court ordered the museum to preserve the removed works and remove no others, pending a full ruling
items.title: Colombian court orders National Museum to keep works the government removed
items.why: A Bogotá family court on 19 October ordered Colombia's National Museum to keep the works the Culture Ministry removed, and to take down no others, pending a full ruling. At least 30 pieces on feminism, LGBTQ rights and the 2016 peace deal had been removed.
items.matters: The government says museums must not be instruments of 'political indoctrination'; riot police broke up a protest at the museum on Saturday.
